thesisQuality.note: Record backlog and revenue across electrical infrastructure markets support durable demand, tempered by project execution economics.

financialOperatingMomentum.note: Record revenue, net income, EBITDA and backlog with strong liquidity show broad operating acceleration; margin quality is discounted for estimate effects.

marketValuationOpportunity.note: 27.4x trailing earnings is balanced against triple-digit TTM earnings growth and substantial backlog, but not clearly cheap.

catalystScore.note: Record backlog, healthy bidding pipeline and newly closed electrical acquisitions create identifiable execution catalysts.

governancePower.note: Current SEC proxy supports conventional board/ownership governance; disciplined project selection is stated and current liquidity supports execution, without evidence for exceptional stewardship.

alignment2036.note: Transmission, distribution, electrification and power-intensive C&I infrastructure are durable critical needs.

crossDivisionLeverage.note: T&D and C&I provide two substantial demand engines, with acquisitions expanding C&I geography/capability.

bottleneckControl.note: Specialized electrical construction capacity participates in a real grid buildout constraint, but contractor competition limits exclusive control.

scenarioRobustness.note: Utility T&D plus C&I diversification supports several infrastructure scenarios, while fixed-price project risk remains.

substitutionResilience.note: Specialized field execution and customer relationships create replacement friction, though competing contractors remain credible substitutes.

supplyChainResilience.note: Strong liquidity and project selection support resilience, but labor/material/project dependencies remain meaningful.

pricingPower.note: Gross margin expansion and strong demand indicate some pricing/execution power, but estimate changes contributed 0.9 points to Q2 margin and fixed-price exposure limits confidence.

risk.note: Moderate risk from fixed-price execution, cancelable backlog and partial nonrecurrence of Q2 margin benefits.

confidence.note: Current issuer operating/balance-sheet evidence, SEC governance and independent market data cover the scoring record; customer concentration and normalized margin remain partial unknowns.

thesis: MYR is converting grid/electrification demand into record backlog and earnings with strong liquidity, while project-estimate volatility limits confidence in peak margins.
keyRisk: Fixed-price execution or backlog conversion disappoints as favorable estimate/closeout effects normalize.
nextCatalyst: Q3 2026 results and backlog/margin conversion after the July acquisitions.
